facts.fact: 作者开篇规划本章：先谈 surprises 之一般与哲学探究中出现的两类 surprise——perplexities 与 illuminations；再论 inquiring 使 conversation partner 面对 ordinary surprises 时 suspend judgment、be courageous and lighthearted；末谈 inquiring 如何训练我们把 surprise 视作从 perplexity 走向 illumination 的契机——这种 inquiring cast of mind 在 inquisitive children、comedians 与 mathematicians 身上同样 discernible。
facts.anchor: about the kinds of surprises—perplexities and illuminations—that emerge during the process

facts.fact: 作者先界定 surprise（事件出乎意料地发生、the pronoun without an antecedent，名字须 “grow some legs” 才能 “hurry” 去 “catch up”），再举三例：joke 的 punch line 恰在此刻到来；friend 不先打电话、恰在你吃晚饭时 popping in；婚姻之终——妻子未料丈夫会 “pull a Bertrand Russell”：going off on a bike ride，suddenly realizing he’s not in love with his wife，回来要求 divorce。
facts.anchor: going off on a bike ride, suddenly realizing he’s not in love with his wife, and coming back to ask for a divorce

facts.fact: 作者指出他所关注的 surprise 是让人得知先前不自知的自己：这类 surprise 或使人 perplex（自以为知道实则不知），或带来 illumination；二者有自然序列——perplexity 在先、illumination 在后，先要为关乎自己的要事 bewildered，才谈得上对自我理解之性质与程度的惊讶；他把第一类表述为一段自白（Before this inquiry, I knew for certain... 而此问之来 I didn’t see coming，如今 I’m stirred up, turned about, bewildered）。
facts.anchor: There’s a natural sequence to these two kinds of surprises, with perplexity coming before illumination.

facts.fact: 作者以 Pride and Prejudice 中的 Elizabeth Bennett 例示 bewilderment：她刚收到 Darcy 的 letter，遂有 “Till now, I never knew myself” 的 declaration——她发现对他人的道德判断建基于对自身 self-worth 的 overvaluation 且 woefully inaccurate；她渴望却不知如何得出更 considered 的自我观，其 plight reminiscent of Meno。
facts.anchor: She has just received a letter from Darcy, and the fresh revelations contained in the letter arrest her.

facts.fact: 作者描述第二类 surprise——self-illumination 之 flash：第一问 disclose 出对的问题，而实际抵达的 answer 亦未及预料；philosophical guide 与 conversation partner 同时认出此即答案、同时 discover the same thing；且 nothing revealed can be taken back——此刻认出自己带来 lightness 与 joy，如同开始 “get used to” 一个新名字、听见自己的名字被更 resonantly and harmoniously 地念出。
facts.anchor: The beautiful realization is that nothing revealed can be taken back.

facts.fact: 在 “The Cultivation of Lightness” 一节，作者论学 inquiry 之益在准备面对 everyday life 的 ordinary surprises：失度反应一端是把意义抬上 positive scale 之顶——trifle of a surprise gift 使人 overjoyed 至 “losing ourselves”；另一端是 startled or shocked，视事件 creep 成 threat，乃至 disappointed、frightened、horrified、paralyzed；他引 Ian Prinsloo 语——children 对 surprises positively “hungry”，而多数 adults 或 titillated and entranced（寻找 “a fix”）或 turned off and cowed——两极皆是 lost a kind of allostasis；故当 cultivate 轻盈回应之品格：inquiring 先训练 suspend judgment、keep composure——如 smiling softly、being in on a joke、reading Alice in Wonderland。
facts.anchor: Ian Prinsloo once told me, are positively “hungry for surprises.

facts.fact: 作者列举随之 invoke 的 virtues：courage（在 unknowing 中 stand firm 而不逃）、temperance（不急于 through with the experience）、patience、discernment；反例是 Thebes 王 Kreon——out of fury 将 Antigone imprisons——以及 self-righteous man 与 diffident and meek；正面则是像 reed 般 bend without breaking，越练越 buoyant and balletic、pliable and flexible。
facts.anchor: So, that unlike the too rigid Kreon, the king of Thebes who, out of fury, imprisons Antigone

facts.fact: 在 “An Inquiring State of Mind” 一节，作者对比两种词汇：wrong vocabulary 把人生当作 “problem” 去 “solve”、“broken part” 去 “fix”、“illness” 待 “diagnosis” 与 “treatment”、“conditions” 去 “cope”、需 “expertise” 去 “addressed”“monitored”“managed”；inquiring 之词则 simpler——be puzzled、curious、nearly bemused、disinterestedly interested，仿佛问题可 viewed from above；此心境如 mathematician、curious child、engrossed reader。结语：时代 unsettled 则不容 smugness、unceasing doubt 或 cowardice；fellow inquirers 可凭 good fortune 与 good practice 出 doubt 入 self-understanding——最终 hit upon 的 right answers 会 stretch and enliven 我们、illuminating our lives in wider and wider circles，使人 come to rest 于 gentle amusement：The right answer certainly feels like belonging。
facts.anchor: taking human life as if it were a “problem” to be “solved”; a “broken part” to be “fixed”;
